newsitem.title: USA: US PLAINS FED CATTLE TRADE LIGHT AT $64 - FEEDLOTS.
newsitem.headline: US PLAINS FED CATTLE TRADE LIGHT AT $64 - FEEDLOTS.

text.p: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade on Monday was slow at $64.00 per cwt, unchanged from sales late last week, feedlot sources said.
About 300 steers likely to grade select and choice sold in Kansas, sources there said. There were no reported sales in the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma region, sources said.
Bids ranged from $63.00 to $64.00 and were passed by most owners who were asking $65.00 to $66.00.
Fed cattle prices this week were seen shaky amid outlooks for continued weak beef prices following last week's slide and projections for large market-ready cattle supplies, they said.
"The beef market looks sloppy for the week and I wouldn't be surprised to see another couple of dollars come off," said Dave Maher, analyst with Securities Corp of Iowa.

Maher added that despite mixed strength on Monday, beef prices were seen being pressured by weak retail demand, with many retailers said to have enough orders booked for Labor Day holiday promotions at the end of the month.

Beef prices on Monday were quoted up $0.48 per cwt to down $0.08, with 149 fabricated beef loads sold, USDA reported. Heavyweight choice beef was quoted at $103.18, down $0.08 from Friday, the USDA statistics showed.

This week's Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma-area showlist was estimated at 90,000 head by some trade groups, down 17,500 from last week. The estimate puzzled several cattle feeders who said they expected an increase in market-ready cattle. However, more cattle indicated in Kansas and Nebraska showlists offset the decline.
The Kansas showlist was pegged near 101,000 head, up 12,000 from last week and Nebraska market-ready cattle were estimated near 93,000, up 9,000, sources in those areas said.
